cohort: 19 patients who underwent emergency obstetric hysterectomy at a tertiary care hospital in South India over a 3-year period.
finding: The incidence of emergency obstetric hysterectomy was 9.3 per 10,000 live births (1 in 1075 deliveries), with atonic postpartum hemorrhage being the most common indication (47%), followed by abnormal placentation (21%).
gest_age: 68.4% of patients were admitted at >34 weeks gestation, 15.7% between 28-34 weeks, and 15.7% <28 weeks at the time of surgery.
